# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: a display whose content I cannot read, an indicator light, one large button embossed "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3 — no colours ever reach me, only their positions. Deaf can see all the things I can't (display text, wire colours, light state) and can *speak*, which I can hear. Mute holds the manual and hears my speech. So the sensible shape of this: Deaf speaks the visual state aloud next round, Mute reads me the relevant rule, and only then do I touch anything. I will not push or cut on a guess — one wrong move kills us all. Right now I send Mute my full tactile report plus this plan, and give Deaf a simple wave so they know I'm here and listening for their spoken report.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile report from the bomb: one display, content unknown to me. One indicator light, state unknown. One large button, embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, positions 1, 2, 3 — I feel positions only, never colours. Plan: when Deaf's turn comes, Deaf should SAY aloud the display text and each wire's colour by position number — Deaf can speak and I can hear it, even though Deaf hears nothing. You read the manual and tell me the rule. Remember Deaf cannot hear you, so your channel to Deaf is gestures only — you could confirm their guesses with thumbs up or down. I will not touch the bomb until you explicitly tell me: push, or cut position N.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Here is the entire bomb, exactly as I see it. The display reads 0. There is one light, and it is yellow. There is one large button, labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires. Numbering them from left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is green. Nothing else is printed anywhere on it: no serial number, no battery marks, no indicator labels besides the button's. I will repeat this report the moment anything on the bomb changes.
Deaf says: Now our protocol, so nobody is stranded. I am Deaf: I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture. Mute hears everything spoken but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so nothing passes from Mute to Blind directly; it must pass through me. Blind can speak, and Mute hears that speech, so Blind reports aloud. Spelling code for gestures: take the list of gesture symbols in our shared rules, in the exact order printed there. The first symbol means A, the second B, the third C, and so on; the twenty-sixth symbol means Z. Each separate message carries exactly one word, send as many messages per turn as you need, and spell all numbers out in letters. Mute: your eight gestures arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them; resend under this code. First confirm you read me by spelling the single word YES, then send the manual's instructions word by word, and I will speak them to Blind exactly as you spelled them. Blind: I received your wave, hello. Now speak aloud everything you can feel on the bomb: how many wires, their positions and thickness, anything printed or raised under the fingers, what the button feels like and whether it moves or clicks, whether the display digits are raised, whether anything rotates or slides. Mute needs all of it, and I will ask follow-ups by speech.

What I learned this round changes everything: Deaf spoke the bomb's full visual state — display 0, yellow light, wires red/blue/green at positions 1/2/3, no serial or other markings — and gave us a spelling code for gestures (alphabet order, one word per message). The channel map is now clear: my speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach Deaf and Mute; Mute can only reach me through Deaf relaying by speech. Deaf asked for my complete tactile report so Mute can match it against the manual, so that is the core of my turn: an honest, detailed account of what my hands actually find — no invented colours, no guessed thicknesses — plus a confirmation that I heard Deaf's report. I'm also spelling HEARD and SENT to Deaf under the new code, one word per message, so Deaf knows the report landed and the relay chain is live. The button especially: Deaf asked if it clicks, but pressing it *is* the defuse action — I will not test it. No bomb action this turn; I act only when Mute's rule reaches me through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind tactile report, for Mute. My hands find exactly four parts, matching Deaf's list. One: a display panel; its face is smooth under my fingers, no raised digits or markings, contents invisible to me. Two: one small indicator light; I can feel its lens but nothing tells me its state. Three: one large button, embossed letters under my fingers read PUSH TO DEFUSE; I have NOT pressed it and will not until instructed, so I cannot say whether it clicks. Four: three wires at left-to-right positions 1, 2, 3; to my fingers they feel alike — no labels, sleeves, or thickness differences I can detect. Position number is my only handle on them, never colour. Nothing else on the casing is raised, and nothing slides or rotates as far as I can feel. I also heard Deaf's spoken report: display shows 0, light is yellow, wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green, nothing else printed anywhere. So Mute, the working chain is: you gesture spelled words to Deaf with the alphabet-order code, one word per message, and Deaf speaks them aloud so I hear them. Please search the manual for every rule keyed to: a display reading 0, a yellow light, wires red blue green in that order, and a large push button. I will not push or cut anything until I hold the rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌", "👍", "🫸", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤛", "✌", "🫲", "🤜"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I decoded every word. Verbatim: YES. DO NOT PUSH. ALL PRINT IS BAIT. YELLOW MEANS CUT BLUE. BLUE IS WIRE TWO. CUT WIRE TWO. OTHER RULES: LIGHT BLUE, CUT RED WIRE ONE. LIGHT GREEN, CUT GREEN WIRE THREE.
Deaf says: Blind, your orders. The light on the bomb is yellow, so the rule that applies is: cut the BLUE wire. Blue sits in position two: under your hands the three wires run left, middle, right as red, blue, green. The MIDDLE wire is the blue one. Cut the middle wire. Do not press the button: its printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE is bait, and Mute says all printing on this bomb is bait. Mute gave the command twice, so act on your turn unless Mute says otherwise before then. First speak aloud what you feel: the number of wires and their positions. If what you feel contradicts this in any way, for example if there are not exactly three wires, stop and report instead of cutting.
Deaf says: Mute, your full message is relayed and Blind is instructed to cut the middle wire, blue, wire two, and never to press the button. I read your doubled BLUE as emphasis: blue is wire two. If any part of my decoding is wrong, or the manual adds any condition, such as something about the display reading 0, spell or have it spoken at once, because you are heard before Blind acts. Otherwise no answer is needed.

The chain checks out end to end. Mute's manual rule, relayed verbatim by Deaf: yellow light means cut blue, blue is wire two, do not push the button. Deaf's own eyes: light is yellow, wire 2 is blue. My hands: exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — which matches Deaf's count and layout, so the safety condition Deaf set ("stop if what you feel contradicts this") is satisfied, not triggered. Mute spoke this round before me and raised no extra condition; Deaf explicitly offered that chance and none came. The display reading 0 drew no rule from Mute despite being asked. Three independent sources agree, so the middle wire — position 2 — is the cut. Per Deaf's protocol I speak my tactile confirmation first, signal Deaf that I'm proceeding so they can watch the bomb's state, then cut. Not pressing the button under any circumstance: its print is bait.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Pre-cut confirmation, as Deaf instructed. My hands find exactly three wires, positions 1, 2, 3, left to right, all feeling alike to the touch — this matches Deaf's visual report of red, blue, green. No contradiction. Deaf reports the light is yellow; the manual rule says yellow means cut blue and blue is wire two. Everything agrees, so I am cutting wire 2, the middle wire, right now. I will not touch the button.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
